description: One file per unexpected behaviour; each is pinned to the check that must fire.

files.why: Z.of_string accepts a sign and a 0x prefix: a negative natural literal would reach the arithmetic. Literals are digits only.
files.msg: bad natural literal

files.why: same, hexadecimal.
files.msg: bad natural literal

files.why: an object with a repeated key is read differently by different tools; refused instead of picking one reading.
files.msg: duplicate key

files.why: a negative de Bruijn index would corrupt the cached loose-variable range.
files.msg: natural number

files.why: a negative projection index raised Invalid_argument from List.nth, exiting with the runtime's own code 2.
files.msg: natural number

files.why: an empty file was accepted: with no declarations there is nothing to accept, and no format was declared.
files.msg: empty file

files.why: a file whose first line is not the meta line does not say which format version it is.
files.msg: meta line

files.why: an exponent of a hundred million would build a number of that many bits: the result is refused (a decline), never computed and never guessed.
files.msg: too large

files.why: a base of a hundred bits to a five-million power overruns the size cap: the result is refused (a decline), never computed and never guessed.
files.msg: too large

files.why: Sort 4 is declared to have type (fun x => Sort 1) Prop, which reduces to Sort 1 while Sort 4 : Sort 5. A quick 'different sorts' verdict after reduction must stay a rejection (found by mutation testing: flipping it to 'equal' survived every test).
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: an unsafe or partial constant is recorded with its type only, and no safe declaration can mention it.
files.msg: unsafe or partial

files.why: Nat.add is redefined as fun a b => a, and the file claims Nat.add 123456789 987654321 = 1111111110 by rfl. With the shortcut keyed on the name the kernel would take the sum from GMP and accept; the fingerprint of the redefined constant is not the genuine one, so literals are unfolded through the file's own definition and the claim fails.
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: claims every n : Nat equals Nat.succ Nat.zero. Structure eta must apply only to structure-like types (one constructor, no indices, not recursive): a mutation that skipped that test accepted this.
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: claims Nat.succ 1 = Nat.succ 2 by rfl. The successor/literal rule decides this one way or the other before anything is unfolded; its 'different' verdict must stay a refusal (a mutation turned it into 'equal' and nothing noticed).
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: claims Nat.succ 1 = 5 by rfl. The successor/literal rule decides this one way or the other before anything is unfolded; its 'different' verdict must stay a refusal (a mutation turned it into 'equal' and nothing noticed).
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: f : Sort 1 -> Sort 1 is declared to have type Sort 0 -> Sort 1. Comparing two binders compares their domains first; a mutation that treated different domains as equal accepted this.
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: Prod.rec (fun a b => a) p0 = p0.1 for an axiom p0 : Nat x Nat holds by structure eta: the stuck major premise is replaced by Prod.mk p0.1 p0.2 before the rule fires. A mutation that skipped the expansion for every constant that is not a constructor refused it (completeness: nothing else noticed).

fun (x : T Nat.zero) => x with T : Bool -> Type: the domain applies T to a Nat. Its type, inferred without looking inside the application, is a sort, and T Nat.zero unfolds to Nat so the lambda's type fits the declared Nat -> Nat. A binder domain must itself be checked; a mutation that only inferred its type accepted this.
files.msg: application type mismatch

files.why: Nat.succ (g Bool.true) with g : Nat -> Nat: the argument g Bool.true has type Nat when inferred without looking inside it, but applies g to a Bool. Arguments are checked, not just typed; a mutation that skipped that accepted this.
files.msg: application type mismatch

files.why: let x : Nat := g Bool.true; x: the value is ill-typed (g applied to a Bool) though its type is Nat. A let value is checked; a mutation that only inferred its type accepted this.
files.msg: application type mismatch

files.why: let x : T Nat.zero := Nat.zero; x: the let's type applies T : Bool -> Type to a Nat. A let type is checked; a mutation that only inferred its sort accepted this.
files.msg: application type mismatch

files.why: outParam is an axiom here, so `outParam Nat` is an ordinary type and the recursor's minor premise must take `outParam Nat`, not `Nat`. The annotation is stripped only when the file's own definition is the identity-like one; a mutation that stripped it for any constant with another kind of declaration accepted the claimed recursor.
files.msg: the type differs from the derivation

files.why: outParam is defined as `fun a => Bool` here: `outParam Nat` is Bool, so the minor premise cannot be claimed to take Nat. Only a definition that returns its first argument makes outParam an annotation; a mutation that accepted any other shape stripped it.
files.msg: the type differs from the derivation

files.why: T (a : Type) := mk (List (T a)): a nested inductive with a parameter, with its two recursors written by hand. The auxiliary type, its recursor and the rebuilding of the derived terms over the parameter are exercised only by a nested type that has one (Lean.Syntax has none): a mutation that rebuilt a lambda over the parameters as a Pi survived every other test.

A and B are two empty propositions declared together, with recursors claimed to eliminate into every Sort. A single empty proposition may (False does); a mutual block of propositions eliminates into Prop only. A mutation that allowed large elimination for mutual blocks accepted the claim.
files.msg: universe parameters differ from the derivation

files.why: String.ofList is an axiom Nat -> String here and the file compares the literal "a" with String.ofList 5. A literal expands through the file's own String.ofList only when it has type List Char -> String (there is no String.mk here either), so the comparison has no meaning and is refused for that reason; a mutation that accepted the constant when either its universe parameters or its type fit expanded the literal anyway and failed later, for another reason.
files.msg: string literal: the environment has no String.ofList or String.mk of type List Char -> String

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: isRec true on a type that is not recursive. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: claimed isRec of T differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: isReflexive true. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: claimed isReflexive of T differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: numNested 1. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: claimed numNested of T differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: numIndices 1. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: claimed numIndices of T differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: the recursor's 'all' lists another type. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: T.rec: 'all' differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: two minor premises. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: T.rec: parameter, index, motive or minor counts differ from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: no computation rule. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: T.rec: number of rules differs from the derivation

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: the K flag. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: T.rec: the K flag differs from the derivation

files.why: an inductive block with no types.
files.msg: empty inductive block

files.why: A takes a universe parameter and B none, in one block.
files.msg: inductive block: universe parameters differ between types

files.why: A has one parameter and B none, in one block.
files.msg: inductive block: number of parameters differs between types

files.why: A's 'all' lists only A although B is declared with it.
files.msg: inductive block: 'all' is not the block

files.why: A : Type and B : Prop in one mutual block: the types must live in one universe.
files.msg: mutually inductive types must live in the same universe

files.why: an expression refers to level 5, which was never defined.
files.msg: dangling

files.why: name 1 is defined twice.
files.msg: defined twice

files.why: Quot declared in a file with no Eq: the quotient rules are stated through Eq.
files.msg: quotient: Eq is not declared

files.why: a quotient declaration named Foo: only Quot, Quot.mk, Quot.lift and Quot.ind exist.
files.msg: quotient: unexpected name

files.why: Quot declared with two universe parameters instead of one.
files.msg: quotient: wrong universe parameters

files.why: Quot declared with type Type instead of {a : Sort u} -> (a -> a -> Prop) -> Sort u.
files.msg: quotient: the type of Quot is not the expected one

files.why: Eq is an inductive family with one constructor, but a one-universe PUnit in disguise: no parameters, no index. The quotient rules need the real Eq.
files.msg: quotient: Eq is not the expected inductive family

files.why: a natural number literal in a file whose Nat is an axiom, not the inductive type.
files.msg: natural number literal: the environment's Nat is not the genuine one

files.why: a string literal in a file with no String.
files.msg: String literal without String

files.why: a.{u} used with no universe level.
files.msg: wrong number of universe levels for a

files.why: Nat.zero applied to an argument: it is not a function.
files.msg: function expected

files.why: an opaque constant of type Nat whose value is Bool.true.
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: T := mk (x : Nat) (PProd T (x = x)): T occurs inside PProd, whose other argument mentions the field x. A nested occurrence's parameters may not contain local variables.
files.msg: invalid nested inductive datatype

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: constructor mk has index 1 though it is the first. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: constructor T.mk has the wrong index

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: the type lists mk but no constructor declaration is given. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: constructor T.mk is listed but not declared

files.why: inductive T := mk (n : Nat) with one claim about the block changed: no recursor is given. Every such claim is derived from the types and constructors and compared; none is trusted.
files.msg: recursor T.rec is derived but missing from the file

files.why: the type A lists B.mk as its constructor but B.mk is declared as a constructor of B.
files.msg: constructor B.mk is listed under another type

files.why: T takes one parameter but the type of T.mk has no binder for it.
files.msg: constructor T.mk: too few parameters

files.why: A and B are declared together but A takes a parameter of type Sort 1 and B one of type Sort 0. All types of a mutual block share their parameters; a mutation that inverted the comparison accepted exactly this.
files.msg: parameters of all inductive types must match

files.why: a.{v} mentions the undeclared universe parameter u inside max. Every parameter must be declared: a mutation that accepted a max when only one side was in scope accepted this.
files.msg: universe parameter out of scope

files.why: a.{v} mentions the undeclared universe parameter u inside imax. Every parameter must be declared: a mutation that accepted a imax when only one side was in scope accepted this.
files.msg: universe parameter out of scope

files.why: Init (toolchain 4.34.0-rc2) never finished this: comparing `Nat.sub A B` with `inst.1 a b` unfolded Nat.sub, which forces whnf of B = a bit-vector value mod 2^32 and peels 2^31 successors. The kernel reduces the projection application first (type_checker.cpp try_unfold_proj_app). Cut with: tools/slice.py init.ndjson out.ndjson _private.Init.Data.Range.Polymorphic.SInt.0.Int32.instRxcHasSize_eq

Init (toolchain 4.34.0-rc2) never finished this: a `grind` certificate check compares `Bool.true` with `Nat.beq 4293853185 (natAbs (leadCoeff p) * 4294965248 - 1112063)` where p is a let-bound variable. The comparison peeled the literal one successor at a time because the term has a free variable; a variable whose value is closed now counts as closed for the arithmetic shortcut. Also: reduce_nat has no free-variable guard (the kernel has none). Cut with: tools/slice.py init.ndjson out.ndjson _private.Init.Data.Char.Ordinal.0.Char.ofOrdinal._proof_3

Lean.Syntax is the one nested inductive in Init (it contains Array Syntax, which contains List Syntax): the auxiliary types, their recursors and the restoring of the derived terms are exercised by nothing else in the quick tests (found by mutation testing: swapping the restore of a lambda for a Pi survived). Cut with: tools/slice.py init.ndjson out.ndjson Lean.Syntax
